mjx_batch_depth_render.structural_limitation: mjx.create_render_context renders one model across nworld worlds, so obstacle geometry, geom type and geom size are shared by every world. The P5 scene bank gives each instance its own analytic primitives, so heterogeneous per-instance scenes cannot share one batched MJX render context even with warp installed.

decision.training_backend: project-side analytic batched pinhole ray caster over the scene bank primitives
decision.why: the scene bank already describes every instance as analytic primitives, so one batched, vmappable, exact ray caster serves depth, MID360, reward clearance and collision with no geometry duplication; this is also the only path that works headless here

p5_03_backend_and_pattern.lidar_backend: project-side analytic batched ray caster over the scene bank primitives
p5_03_backend_and_pattern.why_not_mujoco_lidar_batch_rays_as_the_t: MjLidarJax binds one mjx.Model at construction and MJX renders one model across all worlds, so heterogeneous per-instance obstacle sets cannot share a batched context. The analytic caster uses the same scene bank that collision and reward already use.
p5_03_backend_and_pattern.third_party_cross_check: MjLidarJax on an MJX model built from one scene instance agrees with the analytic caster on the same rays; mujoco.mj_ray agrees to float32 precision
p5_03_backend_and_pattern.mujoco_plane_semantics: MuJoCo bounds plane ray casting by geom size even though dynamic collision treats a plane as infinite; the analytic floor matches the same 100 m margin so parity is exact
